headline: Chips Spark the AI Rebound as Money Rotates Out of Consumer Names
body_html:
Chips led the way on Wednesday as the AI trade regained its footing. Semiconductors climbed 2.25%, the strongest group in our universe, and software added 0.89%. Of the 544 stocks we track, 321 rose and 219 fell, a clear if not lopsided win for buyers. Headlines credited a fresh jolt from SpaceX for lifting sentiment around AI-linked names.

Beneath the surface, money rotated. Energy gained 1.19% and industrials 1.05%, with oil-services firm Weatherford International up 7.75% as Gulf tensions and stalled Iran-US diplomacy kept supply risks in view. Meanwhile consumer shares dropped 1.43%, homebuilders 1.12% and healthcare 0.25%. Capital favored growth and hard assets over household-spending groups, and Winmark and Celsius each fell more than 5%.

Winnebago Industries was the standout, surging 10.66% to top our gainers list, an eye-catching move on a day the consumer group sagged. Nothing in today's headlines explains it, so we won't guess. Zscaler and Okta, up 7.84% and 7.54%, underscored software's bid. With Meta reporting after the close, Thursday opens with chip leadership on trial: rallies this concentrated reward conviction, but leave little cushion if it wavers.

briefs.headline: Airline trims outlook as fuel bites
briefs.body: Southwest Airlines lowered its 2026 profit guidance, blaming higher fuel costs. The warning fits a session in which energy shares were among the leaders, and it shows how the same oil move that helps producers can squeeze carriers' margins.

briefs.headline: Russia open to restarting three-way talks
briefs.body: Vladimir Putin has reportedly agreed to resume peace discussions involving Ukraine and the United States. Reuters carried the report. No firm schedule was cited in our headlines, so markets are likely to treat it as a hopeful signal rather than a breakthrough.

briefs.headline: Gulf unease weighs on regional bourses
briefs.body: Most Gulf stock markets slipped as diplomacy between Iran and the US stalled. Separately, US officials are said to be preparing to pull some personnel from Gulf embassies. Together the reports help explain why energy and oil-services shares stayed in demand.

briefs.headline: Meta in focus ahead of its results
briefs.body: Meta shares rose into the close, with earnings due after the bell. After a session that rewarded AI-linked names, investors will be looking for signs the spending and enthusiasm behind that trade are holding up. Thursday's open will reflect the verdict.

briefs.headline: Salesforce reaches for another deal
briefs.body: Salesforce is reportedly turning to acquisitions again to shore up a softer part of its business. Commentary called the approach sensible. Software had a decent day, with the group up 0.89%, though the move was led by security and identity names.

briefs.headline: Healthcare splits sharply beneath the surface
briefs.body: The healthcare group slipped 0.25%, but the stock-level moves were large. Charles River Labs jumped 9.33% while DexCom fell 6.39% and National HealthCare dropped 4.98%. It was a day for stock-picking inside the sector rather than a group-wide call.
